ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r8.claim: Prostration here means willing submission to God's will, embracing rational and nonrational beings and both worshipful and non-ritual submission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن السجود هنا عبارة عن طواعية ما ذكر تعالى والانقياد لما يريده تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r9.claim: The listed heavenly objects include worshipped angels, the sun worshipped by Himyar, the moon by Kinana, and stars attributed to various Arab tribes; earthly referents include humans, idols, trees, and animals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r9.anchor: والشمس عبدتها حمير. وعبد القمر كنانة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r10.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri reads al-dawābb with a light bā; Abu al-Fadl says this avoids the geminate, as in other lightened doubled forms.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r11.claim: The mention of many people does not conflict with all in the earth prostrating: it can refer specifically to worship prostration, or be separately predicated of people rewarded, with other grammatical analyses also possible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p493/r11.anchor: ولا تعارض بين قوله ومن في الأرض لعمومه وبين قوله وكثير من الناس لخصوصه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses 'many people' as the true people, the righteous and Godfearing, or as a second many upon whom punishment is due; Abū Hayyan calls both analyses weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r1.anchor: من الناس خبرا له أي من الناس الذين هم الناس على الحقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r2.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r2.claim: Janah ibn Hubaysh reads 'and many, great punishment is due to him' with bāʾ instead of thāʾ in kathīr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r2.anchor: وقرأ جناح بن حبيش وكبير حق بالباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows the second 'many' to be coordinated with the earlier list: they prostrate under compulsion through their shadow or when hardship makes them submit; Mujahid likewise says their shadow prostrates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وكثير حق عليه العذاب يحتمل أن يكون معطوفا على ما تقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r4.claim: Other readings include kathīran with an accusative cognate, and ḥaqq with a ḍamma on the initial consonant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r4.anchor: وقرىء وكثير حقا أي حق عليهم العذاب حقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r5.claim: The majority read mukrim as an active participle, while Ibn Abi Abla reads it as a verbal noun meaning honor or honoring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور من مكرم اسم فاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God humiliates whom He wills through decreed misery, while willing honor or humiliation corresponds to people's deeds and beliefs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r6.anchor: ومن أهانه الله كتب عليه الشقاوة لما سبق في علمه من كفره أو فسقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p494/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan detects Mu'tazili doctrine embedded in al-Zamakhshari's explanation.

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.claim: One dating view holds that the surah is Madinan except verses 52–55, which are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.anchor: Some say it is Madinan except for vv. 52–55, which are Makkan (IK)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.claim: Another dating view holds that the surah is Makkan except verses 19–22, which are Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.anchor: others say it is Makkan except for vv.19–22, which are from the Madinan period (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the surah as containing both Makkan and Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.anchor: Most say it is a mix of Makkan and Madinan verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.claim: A tradition calls the surah remarkable because it came at night and by day, on journeys and at home, in war and peace, and includes abrogating and abrogated as well as clear and allegorical verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.anchor: and it has both muḥkam (unambiguous) and mutashābih (symbolic or allegorical) verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.claim: The passage contrasts the misguided and righteous through a garden parable and their respective afterlife reward or punishment.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.anchor: describing their reward or punishment in the Hereafter (vv.8–25)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r7.claim: God knows everyone's behavior and all cases ultimately come before His justice; He distinguishes callers to monotheism from those who distorted religion through innovations, sending disbelievers to Hell and the faithful to Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r7.anchor: God is aware of everyone’s behaviour. None of a person’s word or deed is hidden from Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.claim: The passage revisits monotheism and the Hereafter through human creation, cosmic signs, and divine attributes, contrasts sincere submission with conditional worship and hypocrisy, and concludes with the fate of believers and polytheists.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.anchor: In the coming verses, the subject of monotheism and hereafter discussed earlier is brought up in another way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.claim: Those who deny that benefit and harm are in God’s hands may choose their conduct, but their strategies cannot succeed without His consent; believers and polytheists will face judgement according to belief and deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.anchor: the greatest of their strategies is not going to avail them without God’s consent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p184/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p184/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p184/r5.claim: The universe's objects testify to monotheism through their instinctive Abrahamic submission to God's commands; even the sun, moon, stars, mountains, and cattle follow His laws.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p184/r5.anchor: every object of this universe in its instinctive nature has an Abrahamic temperament

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r1.claim: The sun itself, often worshipped as a deity, daily stands, kneels, and prostrates before its Lord; the moon's phases and the stars' appearances likewise attest submission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r1.anchor: day and night it stands, kneels and prostrates before its Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r2.claim: Shadows of mountains, trees, and animals always lie opposite the sun, symbolically showing that the Creator, not the sun, deserves prostration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r2.anchor: the shadow of everything by its very existence teaches us that it is not the sun which is worthy of prostration but in fact its creator

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r3.claim: This proof of monotheism is an insinuation rather than a formal logical argument, so it is appreciated by those who reflect on the universe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r3.anchor: This argument in favour of monotheism is in the form of an insinuation and hence cannot be grasped by logic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r4.claim: The shadows in 13:15 show that even a person who rebels by choice has a shadow that remains naturally submissive to God and refuses the indignity of bowing to another.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r4.anchor: his own shadows by its very existence detests this attitude

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r5.claim: The passage in 16:48–49 similarly says that created things and their shadows prostrate, alongside all living beings and God's non-arrogant angels.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p185/r5.anchor: all living beings in the heavens and the earth prostrate to God only and the angels of God too

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r1.claim: Unlike nonintentional creation, many people freely submit to God, while others misuse the honor of free choice and disgrace themselves by rejecting truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r1.anchor: many people who out of their free will and intention submit to His directives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r2.claim: Though the universe serves humans, its objects will not accept being worshipped by them; humans, God's best creatures and vicegerents, abase themselves by worshipping inferior deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r2.anchor: they worship deities which are much below their status

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r3.claim: The threatened people merit punishment because they have disgraced themselves and tried to belittle their Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r3.anchor: they disgraced themselves and also tried to belittle their Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r4.claim: Human rank depends on conduct: God preserves or elevates it when people meet moral standards, and lets them fall toward what they chose; 4:115 expresses this practice and assures the Prophet that he cannot save them after decisive proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r4.anchor: their rank and status are kept intact by God and even increased

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r5.claim: Monotheism is humanity's defining distinction; rejecting it makes people lower than the lowliest creation and out of harmony with the universe, even their own shadows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p186/r5.anchor: their own shadow is in discord with them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r1.claim: Verse 24:41 treats the same subject as 22:18: everything in the universe glorifies God; its observable form testifies to obedience while its inner form praises and exalts Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r1.anchor: Exactly the same subject as the one raised in this verse has been discussed in verse 18 of Sūrah al-Ḥajj.

BURSEVI:v6p11/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11/r1.claim: Alam tara is glossed as “did you not know,” addressing one whose characteristic is knowledge.
BURSEVI:v6p11/r1.anchor: ألم تعلم يا من من شأنه العلم

BURSEVI:v6p11/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11/r2.claim: The prostration of all in heaven and earth means submission to God’s governance and will, whether beings obey willingly or are compelled.
BURSEVI:v6p11/r2.anchor: أي : ينقاد لتدبيره ومشيئته الملائكة والجن والإنس مطيعا أو عاصيا

BURSEVI:v6p11/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11/r3.claim: Bursevī distinguishes chosen prostration, for which humans are rewarded, from compelled submission; the verse uses prostration metaphorically because disbelievers, rebellious jinn, animals, and inanimates do not perform ritual worship.
BURSEVI:v6p11/r3.anchor: شبه الانقياد بأكمل أفعال المكلف في باب الطاعة وهو السجود إيذانا بكمال التسخير والتذلل وإنما حمل على المعنى المجازي

BURSEVI:v6p11/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11/r4.claim: The sun, moon, and stars prostrate through their courses, risings, and settings that benefit people.

BURSEVI:v6p11/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11/r5.claim: Mountains prostrate by the springs that God runs through them and the minerals they produce.

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r1.claim: Trees submit through shade and fruit, and animals through their wondrous construction; every creature submits in its created, sustained, healthy, or sick condition, believer or sinner.

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r2.claim: Many people prostrate in chosen worship; the phrase is raised by an omitted predicate, since making it governed by the preceding verb would mix literal and metaphorical senses.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r2.anchor: فهو مرتفع بمحذوف لا بالمذكور وإلا يلزم الجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r3.claim: The Taʾwīlāt says people of gnosis worship by choice, while inanimates, the unintelligent, and irreligious people submit through need.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r3.anchor: قال في "التأويلات" : أهل العرفان يسجدون سجود عبادة بالإرادة

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r4.claim: Kāshifī says every atom is humble and submissive to God through the testimony of its state, which is more eloquent than speech.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (همه ذرات عالم مرخدايرا خاضع وخاشعند بدلالت حال

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r5.claim: The other multitude has punishment decreed because of disbelief and refusal to obey.

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r6.claim: Kāshifī says this is the sixth Qurʾanic prostration by scholarly consensus; the Futūḥāt calls it the prostration of witnessing and reflection, urging worshippers to join the first group and draw near.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r6.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (اين سجدة ششم است باتفاق علما ازسجدات قرآن

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r7.claim: The devotional couplet says the taste of prostration and obedience before God is sweeter than a hundred worldly fortunes.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r7.anchor: ذوق سجده وطاعتي يش خدا خوشتر باثيد زصد دولت ترا

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r8.claim: Bursevī says the first multitude is small beside the second: people of beauty are fewer than people of majesty, about one in a thousand.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r8.anchor: يقول الفقير : الكثير الأول كثير في نفسه بالنسبة إلى الكثير الثاني إذ أهل الجمال

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the single person upon truth is the great majority.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن الواحد على الحق هو السواد الأعظم

BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r10.claim: Some say a group is few when counted but many when they gather and display their strength.
BURSEVI:v6p11#2/r10.anchor: وعن بعضهم : قليل إذا عدوا كثير إذا شدوا أي أظهروا الشدة

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r1.claim: God humiliates a person whose misery He decreed eternally, according to His knowledge that the person would choose evil.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r1.anchor: {يهن الله} يهنه الله : بالفارسية(خوار كرداند) بأن كتب عليه الشقاوة

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r2.claim: No one can honor such a person by granting him everlasting felicity.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r2.anchor: {فما له من مكرم} يكرمه بالسعادة إلى الأبد

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r3.claim: God does as He wills, honoring or humiliating from eternity to eternity.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r3.anchor: {إن الله يفعل ما يشآء} من الإكرام والإهانة من الأزل إلى الأبد

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r4.speaker: النيسابوري
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r4.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī offers three reasons disbelievers outnumber believers: God shows independence from their obedience, the rarity of believers makes their honor clear, and preserving the beloved among many enemies displays divine aid.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r4.anchor: قال الإمام النيسابوري رحمه الله في "كشف الأسرار" : جعل الله الكفار أكثر من المؤمنين ليريهم أنه مستغن عن طاعتهم

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r5.claim: The cited reports say ninety-nine of every thousand are among the people of wrath and one is taken for Paradise; another compares the people of mercy to a white hair on a black ox.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r5.anchor: وأهل الغضب تسع وتسعون من كل ألف واحد يؤخذ للجنة كما ورد في الصحيح

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r6.claim: The answer is that the proportion concerns humans alone; when angels, houris, and youths are included, the people of mercy are more numerous than the people of wrath.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r6.anchor: قلنا هذه الكثرة بالنسبة إلى بني آدم وأما أهل الرحمة بالنسبة إليهم وإلى الملائكة والحور والغلمان فأكثر من أهل الغضب

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r7.claim: The text describes a narrowing spiritual hierarchy: most people disbelieve, then most believers sin, and the rarest reach obedience, asceticism, love, and union; the aim of creation is the perfect human.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r7.anchor: والتحقيق أن المقصود من النشآت كلها ظهور الإنسان الكامل وهو واحد كالألف

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r8.claim: The rare person of union gains true honor by annihilating the self in God, the real station of prostration, and cannot be overcome even if the world seeks to humiliate him.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r8.anchor: فهو أعز من الكبريت الأحمر والمسك الأذفر وهو الذي أكرمه الله بكرامة لم يكرم بها أحدا

BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r9.speaker: الله
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r9.claim: The sacred report says whoever opposes or harms one of God’s friends has declared war on Him; God aids His friends and leaves their opponent humiliated.
BURSEVI:v6p11#3/r9.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله : "من عادى لي وليا فقد بارزني بالمحاربة"

RAZI-FULL:v23p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p17/r1.claim: One reading has حق with ḍamma, while another reads حقا, making it an accusative emphasis that the punishment truly applies.

RAZI-FULL:v23p17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p17/r2.claim: مكرم is also read with fatḥa on rāʾ, with the sense of honoring or showing honor.

RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r6.claim: Here رؤية means knowing: people know this from God's report, not from having seen the prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r6.anchor: أنها العلم أي ألم تعلم أن الله يسجد له

RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls the best explanation of cosmic prostration obedient submission: created things accept God's acts without resistance, resembling obedience; he compares this with verses on creation's submission and praise.
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج أجود الوجوه في سجود هذه الأمور

RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r8.claim: Although all are naturally subject to God, rebellious people refuse prostration outwardly; believers submit both inherently and outwardly, explaining why only many people are singled out.
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r8.anchor: بعضهم تمرد وتكبر وترك السجود في الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r9.claim: One parsing detaches this phrase: the first prostration means submission, the second worship; another makes كثير من الناس a subject with omitted predicate ‘rewarded’; a third repeats كثير to magnify the number deserving punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r9.anchor: قامت الدلالة على أنه لا يجوز استعمال اللفظ المشترك في معنييه جميعا

RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r10.claim: Those who allow a homonym to carry two senses take rational beings' prostration as worship and inanimates' as submission; opponents say the word is used twice with these respective senses.
RAZI-FULL:v23p17#2/r10.anchor: من يجوز استعمال اللفظ المشترك في مفهوميه جميعا

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r1.claim: The general wording in 13:15 includes people, but mentioning many people separately prevents the mistaken inference that all humans prostrate as all angels do.
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r1.anchor: لو اقتصر على ما تقدم لأوهم أن كل الناس يسجدون

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r2.claim: Under that reading, those who refuse prostration are the many people for whom punishment is due.

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r3.claim: A second explanation is that every contingent being depends on the Necessary Being for existence at its beginning and continuation; this intrinsic need is deeper humility than the physical gesture of prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r3.anchor: كل ما سوى الله تعالى فهو ممكن لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r4.claim: Al-Qaffāl applies this dependence to the verse: contingent things are humbled before God and confess need for his bringing them into existence, linking it with 17:44.
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r4.anchor: فجميع الممكنات ساجدة بهذا المعنى لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r5.claim: Mujāhid's third explanation is that things prostrate through their shadows, as in the verse about shadows inclining in prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r5.anchor: أن سجود هذه الأشياء سجود ظلها

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r6.claim: In a report through ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says many people affirm God's oneness, while those due punishment do not.
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وكثير من الناس يوحده

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says many people are in Paradise, supporting the analysis that كثير من الناس is a subject with an omitted predicate.
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r7.anchor: وروى عنه أيضا أنه قال وكثير من الناس في الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r8.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v23p19/r8.claim: Others pause after كثير من الناس and start a new sentence: many others deserve punishment because they refuse and abstain from prostrating.

STUDYQURAN:22:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r1.claim: The entire created world prostrates, not only human beings; the Quran also describes worship by beings other than angels and humans.
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r1.anchor: The prostrating of the whole created world, not just human beings, is also mentioned in 13:15

STUDYQURAN:22:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r2.claim: Prostration denotes both physical action and the humble state of worship that the action signifies.
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r2.anchor: Prostration signifies not only the physical action, but also the very state of humble worship that prostration suggests (R).

STUDYQURAN:22:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r3.claim: The punishment having come due means that it is deserved.
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r3.anchor: The punishment has come due means that it is deserved (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:22:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r4.claim: The structure that none can ennoble whom God disgraces parallels statements about God's guidance, help, and abandonment.
STUDYQURAN:22:18/r4.anchor: The structure of Whomsoever God disgraces, none can ennoble is similar to such other Quranic statements

TAB-FULL:v16p487/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r1.claim: “Do you not see” means know with the heart; heavenly beings include angels, and earthly beings include jinn and other creatures.
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r1.anchor: ألم تر يا محمد بقلبك، فتعلم أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات من الملائكة، ومن في الأرض من الخلق من الجن وغيرهم

TAB-FULL:v16p487/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r2.claim: Their prostration is that of their shadows as the sun rises and declines and each shadow shifts.
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r2.anchor: وسجود ذلك ظلاله حين تطلع عليه الشمس وحين تزول، إذا تحول ظل كل شيء، فهو سجوده

TAB-FULL:v16p487/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the prostration of all these things is their shadows.
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السموات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب} قال: «ظلال هذا كله»

TAB-FULL:v16p487/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r4.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
TAB-FULL:v16p487/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says every star, sun, and moon prostrates when it sets, remains so until permitted to turn right, and then returns toward its rising place.

TAB-FULL:v16p488/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p488/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p488/r1.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers in God.

TAB-FULL:v16p488/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p488/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p488/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses the many people as believers.

TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r1.claim: Many people deserve God's punishment for disbelief, while their shadows still prostrate to Him.

TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the condemned person still prostrates along with his shadow.

TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r3.claim: On Mujāhid's reading the second كثير is coordinated with prostrating believers and حق عليه العذاب modifies it; alternatively it is an independent subject whose punishment implies refusal to prostrate.

TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r4.claim: If outside the prostrating group, كثير is raised by the pronoun in حق عليه; this means many refused prostration, as their punishment shows disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v16p488#2/r4.anchor: وكان معنى الكلام حينئذ: وكثير أبى السجود

TAB-FULL:v16p489/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p489/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p489/r1.claim: God may abase or honor whom He wills because creation and command belong to Him; the following continuation rejects a reading opposed by the authoritative readers.
TAB-FULL:v16p489/r1.anchor: إكرام، وذلك قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لإجماع الحجة

TAB-FULL:v16p489/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p489/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p489/r2.claim: Some read مكرِم as “one who honors,” but Ṭabarī rejects this vocalization because authoritative readers agree against it.
TAB-FULL:v16p489/r2.anchor: إكرام، وذلك قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لإجماع الحجة

TABATABAI:22:17-24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-24/r1.claim: After listing competing groups, the passage says God witnesses and judges them on Judgment Day; even those who refuse outward prostration are inwardly subdued, then their rewards and punishments follow.
TABATABAI:22:17-24/r1.anchor: بيان بعد ما ذكر في الآيات السابقة اختلاف الناس واختصامهم في الله سبحانه بين تابع ضال يجادل في الله بغير علم

TABATABAI:22:17-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r4.claim: The address apparently applies to anyone capable of being addressed, and seeing means knowing; alternatively it may address the Prophet specifically and mean inward vision.
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r4.anchor: الظاهر أن الخطاب لكل من يرى ويصلح لأن يخاطب

TABATABAI:22:17-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r5.claim: Since the list includes nonrational things, prostration means their ontological abasement under God's majesty and dominion.
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r5.anchor: وتعميم السجدة لمثل الشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال من غير أولى العقل دليل على أن المراد بها السجدة التكوينية

TABATABAI:22:17-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r6.claim: This ontological submission includes every human, believer and disbeliever, since no one is exempt from existential subjection.
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r6.anchor: شاملا لنوع الإنسان من مؤمن وكافر

TABATABAI:22:17-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r7.claim: Though heaven and earth themselves are not separately listed, all upper and lower creatures, rational and nonrational, continually submit to God necessarily in their existence.
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r7.anchor: وعدم ذكر نفس السماوات والأرض في جملة الساجدين مع شمول الحكم لهما في الواقع يعطي أن معنى الكلام أن المخلوقات العلوية والسفلية

TABATABAI:22:17-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r8.claim: Because all humans were already included in ontological submission, this many prostrate in a second, voluntary and ritual sense by falling to the ground to express servanthood.
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r8.anchor: وإسناد السجود إلى كثير من الناس بعد شموله في الجملة السابقة لجميعهم دليل على أن المراد بهذا السجود نوع آخر من السجود

TABATABAI:22:17-18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r9.claim: This contrasting phrase stands for those who refuse to prostrate; naming their deserved punishment instead shows it as the consequence of their own action and prepares for the humiliation that follows.
TABATABAI:22:17-18/r9.anchor: المقابلة بينه وبين سابقه تعطي أن معناه

TABATABAI:22:18-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r1.claim: By God's will, refusal to prostrate brings punishment and an abasement never followed by honor; all good belongs to God, and no one else can give what he withholds.
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r1.anchor: وهو إهانة ليس بعده إكرام أبدا

TABATABAI:22:18-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r2.claim: This phrase is an indirect assertion of universal power and explains the punishment and irreversible humiliation of those arrogant toward prostration.
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r2.anchor: كناية عن عموم القدرة وتعليل لما تقدمه من حديث إثباته العذاب للمستكبرين عن السجود له وإهانتهم إهانة لا إكرام بعده

TABATABAI:22:18-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r3.claim: The passage connects God's final separation of disputants to the contrast between universal created submission and humans who either worship openly or arrogantly refuse and are humiliated.
TABATABAI:22:18-19/r3.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن للآية اتصالا بما قبلها

TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r1.claim: A report preserved in al-Tawḥīd has the speaker concede that healing and admission to Paradise occur when God wills, rather than when the person chooses.
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r1.anchor: عبد الله بن الميمون القداح عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عليهما السلام وفيه فيدخلك حيث يشاء أو حيث شئت

TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r2.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r2.claim: Al-Riḍā says that will is an attribute of action, and that whoever claims God has always been willing and choosing is not a monotheist.
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r2.anchor: إلى سليمان بن جعفر الجعفري قال قال الرضا عليه السلام المشيئة من صفات الأفعال

TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads al-Riḍā’s wording as identifying will and choice: in humans, choice describes acting knowingly, while will names that agency when action necessarily follows.
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r3.anchor: تلويح إلى اتحاد الإرادة والمشيئة وهو كذلك فإن المشيئة معنى يوصف به الإنسان

TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r4.claim: Divine will is an attribute of action inferred from the act or its causes, not an essential attribute; saying God willed something means He did it, or prepared its causes, knowing it best.
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r4.anchor: هو وصف خارج عن الذات طارئ عليه، ولذلك لا يتصف تعالى بها كأتصافه بصفاته الذاتية

TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r5.claim: If will is distinct from God's essence yet eternal, it posits an uncreated entity alongside Him and conflicts with monotheism.
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r5.anchor: كان لازمه إثبات شيء أزلي غير مخلوق له معه وهو خلاف توحيده

TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r6.claim: Defining will as knowledge of what is best avoids the problem by reducing it to divine knowledge, but then there is no basis to count it as another attribute beyond life, knowledge, and power.
TABATABAI:22:17-24#2/r6.anchor: ولا محذور فيه غير أن عد الإرادة على هذا صفة أخرى وراء الحياة والعلم والقدرة لا وجه له

TABRISI:22:16-18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:16-18/r10.claim: The Prophet is addressed, while all morally responsible people are intended; “Have you not seen?” means “Have you not known?”
TABRISI:22:16-18/r10.anchor: ثم خاطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به جميع المكلفين فقال

TABRISI:22:16-18/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:16-18/r11.claim: Rational beings in the heavens and earth prostrate to God; the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and animals also prostrate through submission and compliance with their Creator.
TABRISI:22:16-18/r11.anchor: وصف سبحانه هذه الأشياء بالسجود وهو الخضوع والذل والانقياد

TABRISI:22:16-18/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:16-18/r12.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers; the sentence then restarts with the many for whom punishment is decreed.
TABRISI:22:16-18/r12.anchor: يعني المؤمنين الذين يسجدون لله تعالى وانقطع ذكر الساجدين

TABRISI:22:16-18/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:16-18/r13.claim: Those punished are people who refuse to prostrate and do not affirm God’s oneness.
TABRISI:22:16-18/r13.anchor: أي ممن أبى السجود ولا يوحده سبحانه

TABRISI:22:16-18/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r14.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:22:16-18/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the punishment clause implies “many refused to prostrate,” since punishment is deserved only through abandoning prostration.
TABRISI:22:16-18/r14.anchor: قال الفراء: قوله وكثير حق عليه العذاب يدل على أن المعنى وكثير أبى السجود

TABRISI:22:16-18/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:16-18/r15.claim: Whoever God makes wretched and sends to Hell has no one to honor him with happiness and Paradise, since God alone controls punishment and reward.
TABRISI:22:16-18/r15.anchor: بأن يشقيه ويدخله جهنم فما له من مكرم بالسعادة أي بإدخاله الجنة لأنه لا يملك العقوبة والمثوبة سواه

TABRISI:22:16-18/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:16-18/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:16-18/r16.claim: God does as He wills, granting favor to or taking vengeance on both believers and unbelievers.
TABRISI:22:16-18/r16.anchor: من الإنعام والانتقام بالفريقين من المؤمنين والكافرين

THALABI:v7p12/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r1.speaker: أهل الحقائق
THALABI:v7p12/r1.claim: The prostration of inanimate and non-rational things is their abasement, submission, and subjection, shown in the traces of God's craftsmanship that call rational beings to prostrate; a poem says everything bears a sign of God's unity.
THALABI:v7p12/r1.anchor: وقال أهل الحقائق: سجود الجماد وما لا يعقل ما فيها من ذلة الخضوع والتسخير

THALABI:v7p12/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p12/r2.claim: Mujāhid says even people liable to punishment for disbelief have shadows that prostrate to God.
THALABI:v7p12/r2.anchor: وكثير من الناس وكثير حق عليه العذاب بكفره وهو مع ذلك يسجد لله ظله، قال مجاهد:

THALABI:v7p12/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p12/r3.claim: Another view says prostration means submission and inward recognition of what reason necessitates, even if a person disbelieves in other matters.
THALABI:v7p12/r3.anchor: وقيل: يسجد لله أي يخضع له ويقر له بما يقتضيه عقله ويضطره إليه،

THALABI:v7p12/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r4.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p12/r4.claim: Some take the wāw before the many who merit punishment as a conjunction.
THALABI:v7p12/r4.anchor: قالوا: وفي قوله وكثير حق عليه العذاب واو العطف.

THALABI:v7p12/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r5.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p12/r5.claim: Others take the wāw as introducing a new sentence: many merit punishment because they disbelieve and refuse to prostrate.

THALABI:v7p12/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
THALABI:v7p12/r6.claim: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh explains an ellipsis: many people prostrated, while many who deserved punishment refused.
THALABI:v7p12/r6.anchor: حكى لي أبو القاسم بن حبيب عن أبي بكر بن عياش أنه قال: في الآية إضمار مجازها:

THALABI:v7p12/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p12/r7.claim: The phrase means whomever God humiliates.
THALABI:v7p12/r7.anchor: ومن يهن الله أي يهنه الله فما له من مكرم

THALABI:v7p12/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p12/r8.speaker: العامة وإبراهيم بن أبي عيلة
THALABI:v7p12/r8.claim: The common reading has kasrah on the rāʾ, while Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAylah reads fatḥah, taking mukram as ikrām, an abstract verbal noun.
THALABI:v7p12/r8.anchor: قرأه العامة بكسر الراء، وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عيلة : فما له من مكرم بفتح الراء أي إكرام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r4.claim: Alam tara means ‘have you not known’: the seeing intended is by the heart, as explained earlier at 2:243.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ألم تر} ألم تعلم؛ لأن المراد الرؤية بالقلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p323/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes ‘those in the heavens’ as the inhabitants of heaven and ‘those on earth’ as every created kind, including mountains, jinn, and the like.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r1.claim: The author’s preferred meaning of the listed beings’ prostration is their submission, humility, and obedience to what their Lord wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r1.anchor: والصحيح أن المراد بسجودها خضوعها وذلتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says sujūd here is submission to God, an obedience shared by living beings and inanimate things; he cites their response in 41:11.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: السجود هاهنا الخضوع لله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r3.speaker: النحاس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r3.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls submission the sound reading: everything complies in its created state and in what God gives, heals, or afflicts; this is not worship-prostration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r3.anchor: وقال النحاس: هذا القول صحيح بين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r4.claim: A second group says the design and subjection of nonrational beings themselves summon the informed observer to prostrate; the author says this amounts to the first view, since these are their humility before the Creator.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: إن السجود من هذه الأشياء التي هو موات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r5.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r5.claim: A poetic line says hills prostrate under hooves, meaning that they bend or are humbled by the hoofbeats; it evidences figurative sujūd for nonrational things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r5.anchor: الشاعر (¬2): ترى الأكم فيها سجدا للحوافر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the shadows of inanimate things and everything except believers turn as their prostration, as in 13:15; scholars relate this to the sun’s course as a sign.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سجود الجماد وكل شيء سوى المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says every star, sun, and moon prostrates at setting and waits for permission before returning to its rising place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: ما في السماء نجم ولا شمس ولا قمر إلا يقع لله ساجدا حين يغيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r8.claim: On this account all creation truly prostrates to God, though people do not know how; he supports this with other verses about stones, mountains, and creation’s praise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p324/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا فكل شيء مما خلقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r1.speaker: أرباب الأصول
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r1.claim: The theologians of uṣūl say inanimate things cannot reason or distinguish; if they display discernment, God must create that capacity, since it is otherwise impossible in their original nature.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r1.anchor: وقال أرباب الأصول: الجمادات لا تعقل ولا يتميز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r2.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers who worship God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وكثير من الناس} يعني المؤمنين الذين يسجدون لله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r3.claim: Mujāhid says those deserving punishment are unbelievers whose shadows still prostrate; on this reading they too belong among the prostrators.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r4.claim: One view ends the prostration description at ‘the beasts’ and begins a new sentence with ‘many people’; Ibn ʿAbbās says these many are in Paradise, while his ʿAṭāʾ report distinguishes monotheists from those punished for not affirming oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: تم الكلام في وصف الساجدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r5.claim: Another view ends the sentence at ‘many people’ and starts anew: those punished refused to prostrate and are outside the group of prostrators.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون؛ التمام عند قوله {وكثير من الناس}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ argues that ‘punishment became due’ implies that many people refused prostration, since punishment is due only for abandoning it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: قوله {حق عليه العذاب} يدل على أن المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r7.claim: The author prefers the pause after ‘many people,’ the stopping choice of Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Ḥātim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p326/r7.anchor: وهذا القول هو اختيار نافع والكسائي وأبي حاتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses God’s humiliating someone as making him wretched, with no one to help him; Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to say this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: يريد من يشقه الله فما له من مسعد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says this is someone who treats worship of God lightly: God has disgraced and banished him, leaving Hell rather than the honor given to His allies.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r3.claim: God does as He wills among His creatures, granting humiliation or honor, misery or happiness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p328/r3.anchor: أي: في خلقه من الإهانة والكرامة والشقاء والسعادة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r3.claim: Prostration here means being humbled before God and submitting to Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r3.anchor: يسجد له } يذل له، وينقاد له

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r4.claim: All things submit to God in their created state, provision, health, and sickness, whether righteous or sinful, believer or unbeliever.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r4.anchor: كل شيء منقاد لله عز وجل على ما خلقه، وعلى ما رزقه، وعلى ما أصحه وعلى ما أسقمه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r5.claim: Some people submit, while many others are subject to punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r5.anchor: فالبر والفاجر، والمؤمن و الكافر في هذا سواء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r6.claim: If God humiliates someone through disbelief, no one else can honor that person.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r6.anchor: يذله بالكفر { فما له من مكرم } أحد يكرمه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r7.claim: God humiliates whom He wills with disbelief and honors whom He wills with faith.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:17-18/r7.anchor: يهين من يشاء بالكفر، ويكرم من يشاء بالإيمان

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r1.claim: All inhabitants of heaven glorify God, and some on earth prostrate to Him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السموات ومن في الأرض} [الحج: 18] يعني أن جميع أهل السماء يسبحون له وبعض أهل الأرض

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan counts prostration only among Muslims, not polytheists.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r2.anchor: وكان الحسن لا يعد السجود إلا من المسلمين، ولا يعد ذلك من المشركين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says a believer prostrates willingly and an unbeliever unwillingly.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يسجد المؤمن طايعا، ويسجد الكافر كارها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r4.claim: The sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and animals all prostrate to God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r4.anchor: قال: {والشمس والقمر والنجوم} [الحج: 18] كلها. {والجبال والشجر} [الحج: 18] كلها. {والدواب}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r5.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r5.anchor: ثم رجع إلى صفة الإنسان فاستثنى فيه فقال: {وكثير من الناس} [الحج: 18] يعني المؤمنين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r6.claim: Those for whom punishment is due are those who did not believe.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r6.anchor: {وكثير حق عليه العذاب} [الحج: 18] يعني من لم يؤمن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r7.claim: God humiliates a person by admitting him to the Fire.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p358#2/r8.claim: No one can honor such a person by admitting him to Paradise.

QASHANI:22:18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:18/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:18/r1.claim: All celestial and terrestrial kingdoms and counted or uncounted things prostrate through obedience and compliance; their acts and properties are compelled under God's power.
QASHANI:22:18/r1.anchor: من الأشياء بالانقياد والطاعة والامتثال لما أراد الله منها من الأفعال والخواص

QASHANI:22:18/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:18/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:18/r2.claim: Humans alone can follow Satan outwardly despite inward compulsion; many are condemned through eternal decree because satanic traits and misfortune dominate them.
QASHANI:22:18/r2.anchor: ولما لم يمكن لشيء منها إلا للإنسان التابع للشيطان في ظاهر أمره دون باطنه خص عموم كثير من الناس

QASHANI:22:18/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:18/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:18/r3.claim: When God humiliates someone by making them a locus of subjection, wrath, and punishment, no one can honor them; God acts as He wills.
QASHANI:22:18/r3.anchor: { ومن يهن الله } بأن يجعل أهله قهره وسخطه ومحل عقابه وغضبه { فما له من مكرم إن الله يفعل ما يشاء }

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r11.claim: The rhetorical question means either that the addressee perceives this with the heart's eye or that he has heard of it.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r11.anchor: görmedin mi yani kalb gözüyle idrak edemedin mi veya haberin yok mu

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r12.claim: All things in reality prostrate by submitting completely to God's judgment and governance.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r12.anchor: Hakikatte Allah, O’na hep şunlar secde ediyor

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r13.claim: The phrase includes everything above and below, such as angels and souls, and every living and nonliving thing.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r13.anchor: yukarılarda ve aşağıda her kim ve her ne varsa, melâike ve nüfûs, canlı ve cansız her şey

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r14.claim: The named examples of those subject to God include the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and all animals.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r14.anchor: Şems ü Kamer ve nücûm, dağlar ve ağaçlar ve bütün hayvânât

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r15.claim: Many people means a portion of humanity, not everyone or even necessarily a majority; the portion is still substantial.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r15.anchor: insanlara gelince hepsi değil, ekserîsi de değil, bir kısmı, mukabilinden daha çok değilse de haddizâtında bir kesret teşkil eden bir kısmı secde ediyor

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r16.claim: All people are included in the earth's inhabitants insofar as they submit involuntarily to God's coercive effects.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r16.anchor: Gerçi Allah teâlâ’nın te’sîrât-ı cebriyesine, bütün insanlar da ister istemez inkıyad eyler

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r17.claim: Only a portion of people, namely believers, freely submit through obedient prostration, which involves the human will.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r17.anchor: ihtiyar ile alâkadar olan inkıyâd-ı irâdîyi ve secde-i itâati yapan insanların ancak bir kısmıdır ki mü’minlerdir

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r18.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r18.claim: Some commentators take the phrase as a new coordinated clause, supplying an implied 'many people prostrate' to emphasize obedient prostration.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r18.anchor: bazı müfessirîn bu secde-i itâat mânasını ibraz için işbu وَكَثِيرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ kaydının atf-ı cümle kabîlinden olmak üzere ويسجد كثير من الناس takdîrinde olduğunu söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:22:17-18/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r19.claim: Those deserving punishment rebel against God's command in unbelief and disobedience, refusing obedient prostration; they are devils and their human followers.
ELMALILI:22:17-18/r19.anchor: Allah’ın emrine karşı küfr ü isyan ile serkeşlik edip secde-i itâatten istinkâf eylemiştir. Ki bunlar şeytanlar ve şeytanlara uyan insanlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r1.claim: The universe's beings submit to God under necessary laws of obedience; humans are left to free choice as part of their trial and are not universally obedient.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r1.anchor: evrendeki zorunlu itaat yasaları uyarınca Allah’a boyun eğen varlıklara dikkat çekilmekte, insanların ise sınav ortamının icabı olarak hür iradeleriyle baş başa bırakılmaları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r2.claim: As a result, many people obey God and attain salvation, while many others deserve punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:18/r2.anchor: dolayısıyla birçok insan Allah’a itaat edip kurtuluşa ererken nicelerinin de azabı hak etmiş olacağı uyarısı yapılmaktadır

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r1.claim: Gnostics prostrate to God in worship, while rejecters prostrate through every part of themselves as testimony to His existence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r1.anchor: أهل العرفان يسجدون له سجود عبادة ، وأرباب الجحود كل جزء منهم يسجد له سجود دلالة وشهادة

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r2.claim: A cited verse asks whether everything bears a sign pointing to God's oneness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r2.anchor: وفي كل شيء له آية . . . تدل على أنه واحد ؟

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r3.claim: For rejecters, today's clothing is shirk and deprivation, with falsehood and abandonment as its trim; in the afterlife it is pitch and estrangement.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r3.anchor: أما الذين كفروا فلهم اليوم لباس الشرك وطرازه الحرمان ، ثم صدار الإفك وطرازه الخذلان

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r4.claim: Believers' present garment of piety has degrees: avoiding association, disobedience, heedlessness, reliance on other than God, and delight in what is other than Him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r4.anchor: أما أصحاب الإيمان فلباسهم اليوم التقوى ، وتنقسم إلى اجتناب الشرك ثم مجانبة المخالفة

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r5.claim: In the next life, some believers wear silk, others the cloak of love, solitude with God, or spiritual detachment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r5.anchor: وفي الآخرة لباسهم فيها حرير ، وآخرون لباسهم صدار المحبة ، وآخرون لباسهم الانفراد به

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r6.claim: The elect are strangers and the highest class, with no state, station, rank, or place and no servitude to anything brought into being.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r6.anchor: فلا حال ولا مقام ولا منزلة ولا محل وهم الغرباء ، وهم الطبقة العليا

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r7.claim: Their spiritual adornment protects them and conceals their states; they beautify Paradise rather than needing Paradise to adorn them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r7.anchor: التحلية تحصين لهم ، وستر لأحوالهم ؛ فهم للجنة زينة ، وليس لهم بالجنة زينة

QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r8.claim: A cited couplet says that just as a pearl beautifies a face, the beloved's beauty makes the pearl itself beautiful, illustrating their being Paradise's adornment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p314/r8.anchor: وإذا الدر زان حسن وجوه . . . كان للدر حسن وجهك زينا

BURHAN:v1p140/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p140/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p140/r1.claim: The phrase repeats من in Yunus, al-Hajj, al-Naml, and al-Zumar.

BURHAN:v4p411/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p411/r8.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p411/r8.claim: Earlier grammarians say man is primarily for rational beings, while later scholars prefer knowing beings to include God; Sībawayh narrows it to humans, and the angel example prompts the reply that humans are its dominant use.
BURHAN:v4p411/r8.anchor: وضيق سيبويه العبارة فقال هي للأناسي فأورد عليه أنها تكون للملك

BURHAN:v4p411/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p411/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p411/r9.claim: When man is used for non-rational things, either they are treated as rational or they occur mixed with rational beings.
BURHAN:v4p411/r9.anchor: وإذا أطلقت على ما لا يعقل فإما لأنه عومل معاملة من يعقل وإما لاختلاطه به

BURHAN:v3p221/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p221/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p221/r1.claim: Brevity is eloquent when wording is shorter than its usual measure relative to meaning; it displays command of eloquence, and the discussion distinguishes equal wording from compressed wording.
BURHAN:v3p221/r1.anchor: فالوجيز باللفظ أن يكون اللفظ بالنسبة إلى المعنى أقل من القدر 1 المعهود عادة وسبب حسنه أنه يدل على التمكن

BURHAN:v3p221/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p221/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v3p221/r2.claim: The Prophet described his gift as comprehensive, concise speech, offered here as an example of the virtue of verbal concision.
BURHAN:v3p221/r2.anchor: ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم أوتيت جوامع الكلم

BURHAN:v3p221/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p221/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p221/r5.claim: Though the verse applies prostration to all, its unifying sense is submission or compliance.
BURHAN:v3p221/r5.anchor: فإن السجود في الكل يجمعه معنى واحد وهو الانقياد

BURHAN:v3p221/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p221/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p221/r6.claim: Compressed expression can carry extensive meaning; the author lists commands to accept pardon and the guided people's security as examples.
BURHAN:v3p221/r6.anchor: والثاني كقوله ﴿ خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين ﴾ 5 وقوله ﴿ أولئك لهم الأمن

ITQAN:v3p91/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p91/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p91/r6.claim: Some خطاب is general rather than aimed at one listener; its scene is so evident that anyone capable of seeing is included in the address.
ITQAN:v3p91/r6.anchor: لم يقصد بذلك خطاب معين بل كل أحد وأخرج في صورة الخطاب لقصد العموم

ITQAN:v2p346/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p346/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
ITQAN:v2p346/r1.claim: Al-Anbārī says Companions and Successors often used poetry to explain rare or difficult Qur’anic words; critics wrongly accused them of making poetry the Qur’an’s source.
ITQAN:v2p346/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر الأنباري قد جاء عن الصحابة والتابعين كثيرا الاحتجاج على غريب القرآن ومشكله بالشعر

ITQAN:v2p346/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p346/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
ITQAN:v2p346/r2.claim: Al-Anbārī answers that poetry clarifies an unfamiliar Arabic word rather than serving as the Qur’an’s foundation, since the Qur’an declares itself Arabic.
ITQAN:v2p346/r2.anchor: قال وليس الأمر كما زعموه من أنا جعلنا الشعر أصلا للقرآن بل أردنا تبيين الحرف الغريب من القرآن

ITQAN:v2p346/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p346/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p346/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls poetry the Arabs’ register and advises consulting it when an unfamiliar Qur’anic word is unclear.
ITQAN:v2p346/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس الشعر ديوان العرب فإذا خفي علينا الحرف من القرآن الذي أنزله الله بلغة العرب رجعنا إلى ديوانها

ITQAN:v2p346/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p346/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
ITQAN:v2p346/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayd reports that Ibn ʿAbbās answered questions about the Qur’an by reciting poetry, which Abū ʿUbayd explains was evidence for interpretation.
ITQAN:v2p346/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد في فضائله حدثنا هشيم عن حصين بن عبد الرحمن عن عبد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن ابن عباس أنه كان يسأل عن القرآن فينشد فيه الشعر قال أبو عبيد يعني كان يستشهد به على التفسير

ITQAN:v2p346/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p346/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p346/r5.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says he collected many such explanations from Ibn ʿAbbās, especially the questions of Nāfiʿ b. al-Azraq, and presents them in full.
ITQAN:v2p346/r5.anchor: قلت قد روينا عن ابن عباس كثيرا من ذلك وأوعب ما رويناه عنه مسائل نافع بن الأزرق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r1.claim: The rare verb يقتاعها means that the calf climbs or leaps onto the she-camel; it is derived from the expression for a male camel mounting a female.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r1.anchor: يقتاعها يفثعل من قولهم قاع البعير الناقه إذا ضربها يقوعها قوعا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r2.claim: The calf’s irregular movements while trying to make its kneeling mother rise are likened to an Ethiopian climbing a ladder, with limbs rising and falling in violent disorder.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r2.anchor: وشبه بالحبشي في هذه الحالة المخصوصة لما يكون له عند ارتفاعه في السلم من تصعد بعض أعضائه وتسفل بعض على اضطراب مفرط

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r3.claim: A distinctive composite likeness comes from body parts moving in different directions; such configurations are rare and less readily recalled than familiar wheel, mill, or arrow motions, as in lightning likened to a manuscript.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r3.anchor: الاختلاف في جهات الحركات الواقعة في أبعاض الجسم كالتركيب بين أوصاف مختلفة ليحصل من مجموعها شبه خاص

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r4.claim: The shaking-hand mirror simile is novel not merely because the mirror moves rarely, but because its shimmering light undulates from the circumference toward the center, a pattern that requires attentive observation.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p160/r4.anchor: بل النكته المقصودة فيما يتولد من دوام تلك الحركة من الالتماع وتموج الشعاع وكونه في صورة حركات من جوانب الدائرة إلى وسطها

TUSTARI:22:18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:22:18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:22:18/r1.claim: The prostration of the sun, moon, and other things is their knowledge of God expressed through humility and obedience.
TUSTARI:22:18/r1.anchor: سجود هذه الأشياء معرفتها بالحق بالتذلل والانقياد له

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r1.claim: In the second kind of particle relation, a coordinated second noun enters the same governor’s operation as the first, whether nominative, accusative, or governed by a preposition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r1.anchor: يدخل الثاني في عمل العامل في الأول كقولنا : جاءني زيد وعمر و ، ورأيت زيدا وعمرا ،

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r2.claim: Negation, interrogation, and conditional particles apply to a complete predication: they concern an action as attributed to a subject, not an unbound action or entity.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r2.anchor: أن من شأن هذه المعاني أن تتناول ما تتناوله بالتقييد ، وبعد أن يسند إلى شيء . معنى ذلك أنك إذا قلت : ما خرج زيد وما زيد خارج لم يكن النفي الواقع بها متناولا الخروج على الإطلاق ، بل الخروج واقعا من زيد ومسندا إليه .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r3.claim: لا رجل في الدار negates the class’s being in the house; particles such as كأن require both sides of a comparison, while لو and لولا require two clauses.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r3.anchor: ولا يغرنك قولنا في نحو : ( لا رجل في الدار ) أنها لنفي الجنس ؛ فإن المعنى في ذلك أنها لنفي الكينونة في الدار عن الجنس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r4.claim: A particle and verb, or a particle and noun, do not by themselves form a sentence except in vocative use, where an implicit verb such as أريد or أدعو is understood.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p15/r4.anchor: وجملة الأمر أنه لا يكون كلام من حرف وفعل أصلا ، ولا من حرف واسم إلا في النداء نحو : يا عبد الله . وذلك أيضا إذا حقق الأمر كان كلاما بتقدير الفعل المضمر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r1.claim: The wāw called wāw al-ḥāl joins a new independent proposition to the preceding clause; it does not make the two assertions one predication.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r1.anchor: وتسميتنا لها ' واو الحال ' لا يخرجها عن أن تكون مجتلبة لضم جملة إلى جملة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r2.claim: He compares this wāw with the fāʾ in conditional responses: both connect a clause that cannot attach to its antecedent by itself, unlike a clause that links intrinsically.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r2.anchor: فإنها وإن لم تكن عاطفة فإن ذلك لا يخرجها من أن تكون بمنزلة العاطفة في أنها جاءت لتربط جملة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r3.claim: In «جاءني زيد وهو يسرع», the separate pronoun restarts the assertion, like «جاءني زيد، وزيد يسرع»; without wāw, «جاءني زيد يسرع» integrates speed into the coming.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p169/r3.anchor: فجئت بضميره المنفصل المرفوع كان بمنزلة أن تعيد اسمه صريحا فتقول

RUMMANI:v1p102/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r1.claim: Tadmin is a meaning conveyed without explicitly naming it by a noun or attribute; it may be communicated by direct reporting or by inference.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r1.anchor: تضمين الكلام هو حصول المعنى فيه من غير ذكر له باسم أو صفة هي عبارة عنه.

RUMMANI:v1p102/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r2.claim: One kind of implication is built into morphology: calling something known entails a knower, just as calling someone honored entails one who honors.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r2.anchor: فالصفة بمعلوم يوجب أنه لابد من عالم

RUMMANI:v1p102/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r3.claim: Some implications are required by a word's meaning: قاتل entails someone killed, since the sense of killer cannot stand without a victim.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r3.anchor: فكالصفة بقاتل يدل على مقتول من حيث لا يصح معه معنى قاتل

RUMMANI:v1p102/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r4.claim: An implication may also come from customary usage: الكر بستين leaves out dinars because convention supplies the understood unit.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r4.anchor: فكقولهم: " الكر بستين " المعنى فيه بستين دينارا

RUMMANI:v1p102/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r5.claim: All implication is concise expression that dispenses with elaboration when the meaning can be inferred from the wording.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r5.anchor: والتضمين كله إيجاز استغنى به عن التفصيل إذ كان مما يدل دلالة الإخبار في كلام الناس

RUMMANI:v1p102/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r6.claim: Inferential implication is a distinctive feature of God's speech: God misses no valid implication, so His choice of wording indicates every meaning the wording can support; human speakers may intend only its lexical sense.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r6.anchor: فأما التضمين الذي يدل عليه دلالة القياس فهو إيجاز في كلام الله عز وجل خاصة

RUMMANI:v1p102/r7.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p102/r7.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p102/r7.claim: Every verse includes an unstated implication; the basmala teaches beginning acts with blessing and reverence, religious etiquette and Muslim identity, servitude and gratitude for God's greatest favor, and refuge for the fearful.
RUMMANI:v1p102/r7.anchor: وكل آية فلا تخلو من تضمين لم يذكر باسم أو صفة

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r9.claim: Yuhin can mean humiliate; the source groups it with humiliation and the phrase describing a humiliating punishment.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r9.anchor: ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم كقوله سبحانه أيمسكه على هون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r1.claim: The root’s basic sense is humiliation and diminished worth; hawn, with fatḥa on hāʾ, instead means calmness and dignity.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r1.anchor: فأما الهون . بفتح الهاء - فهو السكينة والوقار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r4.claim: In the warning that God may abase someone, the root means humiliation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p638/r4.anchor: والثالث : الذل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

FARRA:v2p218/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p218/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p218/r4.claim: من في السماوات refers to the inhabitants of the heavens; من في الأرض encompasses creatures such as mountains, jinn, and their like.
FARRA:v2p218/r4.anchor: يريد: أهل السموات (ومن في الأرض) يعني كل خلق من الجبال ومن الجن وأشباه ذلك

FARRA:v2p218/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p218/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p218/r5.claim: The many people who prostrate are the obedient; the many for whom punishment is due are those who refused prostration, since punishment follows abandoning obedience.
FARRA:v2p218/r5.anchor: وكثير من الناس) من أهل الطاعة (وكثير حق عليه العذاب) فيقال. كيف رفع الكثير وهو لم يسجد؟

FARRA:v2p218/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p218/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p218/r6.claim: The nominative كثير is licensed by the resumptive reference in حق عليه, which implies refusal; it is as though the predicate said أبى.
FARRA:v2p218/r6.anchor: فالجواب في ذلك أن قوله (حق عليه العذاب) يدل على أنه: وكثير أبى السجود

FARRA:v2p218/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p218/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p218/r7.claim: Accusative وكثيرا is also possible, as in فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة; the nominative likewise appears with resumptive reference, as in the cited verses.
FARRA:v2p218/r7.anchor: ولو نصبت: وكثيرا حق العذاب كان وجها بمنزلة قوله (فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة)

FARRA:v2p219/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p219/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p219/r1.claim: يهن means that God makes someone wretched; such a person has no one to aid him. مكرم may alternatively mean إكرام, honoring.
FARRA:v2p219/r1.anchor: وقوله (ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم) يقول: ومن يشقه الله فما له من مسعد.

FARRA:v2p219/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p219/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p219/r2.claim: مكرم may be read as a verbal noun meaning honoring, rather than a person who honors.
FARRA:v2p219/r2.anchor: وقد تقرأ (فما له من مكرم) يريد: من إكرام.

NAHHAS:v3p90/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p90/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p90/r3.claim: The sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, animals, and many people are coordinated with من, as those who prostrate to God.

NAHHAS:v3p90/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p90/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p90/r4.claim: Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra say accusative coordination would be acceptable, but raising كثير is preferable because it means many abstain from prostrating.
NAHHAS:v3p90/r4.anchor: فزعم الكسائي والفراء أنه لو نصب لكان حسنا ولكن اختير الرفع لأن المعنى وكثير أبي السجود

NAHHAS:v3p90/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p90/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p90/r5.claim: An alternative parses كثير as coordinated with the earlier subjects: all things prostrate by submitting to God's governance of weakness, strength, health, sickness, beauty, and ugliness.
NAHHAS:v3p90/r5.anchor: وفي رفعه قول آخر يكون معطوفا على الأول داخلا في السجود

NAHHAS:v3p90/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p90/r6.speaker: الكسائي والأخفش والفراء
NAHHAS:v3p90/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i, al-Akhfash, and al-Farra explain مكرم in the sense of إكرام, honor or honoring.
NAHHAS:v3p90/r6.anchor: وحكى الكسائي والأخفش والفراء ( ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم )

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r1.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted يسجد, since prostration by rational people is a physical act unlike the obedience or submission meant for nonrational creatures.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه مرفوع بفعل مضمر تقديره: ويسجد له كثير من الناس.

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r2.claim: Alternatively, وكثير من الناس coordinates with the preceding subjects if سجود has the shared sense of submission and obedience for all beings.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r2.anchor: أحدها: أن المراد بالسجود القدر المشترك بين الكل العقلاء وغيرهم

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r3.claim: Coordination is also possible if سجود is a homonym used in both its human and nonhuman senses.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r3.anchor: والتأويل الثاني: أنه مشترك اشتراكا لفظيا، ويجوز استعمال المشترك في معنييه.

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r4.claim: A further coordination analysis combines literal prostration by humans with metaphorical prostration by other beings; the author notes disagreement over these principles.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r4.anchor: والتأويل الثالث: أن السجود المسند للعقلاء حقيقة ولغيرهم مجاز.

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes كثير a subject with an omitted predicate such as مثاب, inferred from its counterpart وكثير حق عليه العذاب; Abū al-Baqāʾ suggests مطيعون or مثابون.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r5.anchor: الثالث من الأوجه المتقدمة: أن يكون " كثير " مرفوعا بالابتداء. وخبره محذوف وهو " مثاب "

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r6.claim: Another analysis makes كثير a subject and من الناس its predicate, meaning the people in the truest sense: the righteous and God-fearing.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r6.anchor: الرابع: أن يرتفع " كثير " على الابتداء أيضا، ويكون خبره " من الناس "

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows كثير to coordinate with the repeated كثير, followed by حق عليه العذاب as its predicate, intensifying the number punished.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r7.anchor: فيعطف " كثير " على " كثير " ثم يخبر عنهم ب { حق عليه العذاب } ذكر ذلك الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r8.claim: The Shaykh calls the two final analyses weak; the author finds the omitted-predicate analysis unhelpful but the repeated كثير defensible because repetition expresses abundance, as in ألف وألف.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r8.anchor: قال الشيخ: بعد أن حكى عن الزمخشري الوجهين الآخرين قال: " وهذان التخريجان ضعيفان "

SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r9.claim: The author says the first of the disputed analyses adds little, but repetition is defensible because it conveys abundance, like عندي ألف وألف.
SAMIN-DURR:22:18/r9.anchor: أما أولهما فلا شك في ضعفه؛ إذ لا فائدة طائلة في الإخبار بذلك./ وأما الثاني فقد يظهر: وذلك أن التكرير يفيد التكثير، وهو قريب من قولهم: " عندي ألف وألف "

SAMIN-DURR:22:18#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
